verdicts.title: Empty-batch short-circuit runs pre_clipping_transform on zeros without NaN/Inf sanitization, so value-dependent transforms emit NaN gradients on empty Poisson rounds
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified on the current tree. (1) packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_helpers.py:121-127 is exactly as claimed: 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums); transformed = pre_clipping_transform(zeros)' followed only by an optional dtype cast -- no torch.nan_to_num. (2) The non-empty path is sanitized: clip_pytree opens with tree_map(torch.nan_to_num(..., nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)) (packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_pytree.py:599-606) and auto_scale_pytree has the identical opener at :463-470; clip_pytree's own docstring lists 'NaN/Inf values: Replaced with zeros before clipping' as a documented edge case, so the empty path bypasses a documented invariant. (3) On the non-empty path the transform is applied per example inside grad_fn (_clipped_grad.py:290) and its output flows into clip_pytree, so the user transform is never evaluated on a synthetic all-zero tree there -- only the empty short-circuit does that. (4) The regression claim holds: git show f59e3c12 (PR #856) replaces 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple)' with 'empty_clipped_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple, pre_clipping_transform, dtype)', so before that commit the empty path could not emit a non-finite value. (5) Reproduced with the repo venv (torch 2.14.0+cu130): with tr = lambda g: tree_map(lambda t: t/global_norm(g), g), clipped_grad(loss, argnums=0, batch_argnums=(1,2), clipping_norm=1.0, pre_clipping_transform=tr) returns ClippedPytree(tensor([1.1542, 1.9901, -0.9160])) on a 4-example batch and ClippedPytree(tensor([nan, nan, nan])) on a (0,3) batch; auto_clipped_grad(R=1.0, ...) behaves identically; gaussian_noise(noise_multiplier=1.0, key=key(0)) on the empty-step output returns NoisedPytree(tensor([nan, nan, nan])), so the NaN is not contained. adaptive_clipped_grad routes through the same helper (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:455-462) though I did not run it (it needs a key= argument I did not wire up); the code path is the same call to empty_clipped_grads_like. Searched for an upstream guard and found none: nothing between empty_clipped_grads_like and clipped() sanitizes, and no test pins finiteness of the empty-batch output. Severity held at medium rather than raised: with the default identity pre_clipping_transform (and with any value-independent transform, including the documented preconditioner-scaling use case) there is no defect at all -- it takes a user-supplied transform whose output depends on the gradient values, plus an empty Poisson draw. Not raised to high/critical for that reason; not dropped to low because when it does fire it silently and permanently NaNs the parameters with no warning or exception.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Non-default config only: functional DP-SGD with a Poisson sampler AND a caller-supplied value-dependent pre_clipping_transform (e.g. tr = lambda g: tree_map(lambda t: t / global_norm(g), g)). On any round where the Poisson draw is empty, clipped_grad / auto_clipped_grad / adaptive_clipped_grad take the empty-batch short-circuit, which calls the transform on an all-zero gradient pytree; 0/0 yields NaN and, unlike the non-empty path, nothing sanitizes it. Reproduced on the current tree (repo venv, torch 2.14.0+cu130): finite ClippedPytree on a 4-example batch, ClippedPytree(pytree=tensor([nan, nan, nan])) on the (0,3) batch, and gaussian_noise on that output returns all-NaN, so the first empty round corrupts the parameters through the optimizer with no warning or exception. With the default identity transform, or any transform that does not divide by a gradient-derived quantity, the path is unaffected. Regression introduced by f59e3c12 (#856); the pre-fix empty path returned plain zeros and could not be non-finite.

verdicts.title: clipped_fun and auto_clipped_fun, the public power-user primitives, have no empty-batch handling at all and die with an opaque error on a zero-length batch
verdicts.reasoning: Verified independently. packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py has no batch-size-zero short-circuit: grepping for empty/batch_size==0 returns only the stats-shaping branch at :326-340 inside _compute_clipping_stats, and the fast path reaches 'vmapped = _vmap(per_example_fn, ...); outputs = vmapped(kernel_clipping_norm, *args, **kwargs)' (:683-688) unconditionally. _auto.py contains no 'empty' occurrence and auto_clipped_fun delegates to the same machinery. Neither module's docstring mentions empty batches, and no test in packages/opaque-engine/tests/clipping/ pins the behavior. By contrast _clipped_grad.py:222-258 has _empty_batch_response precisely 'so downstream buffers stay stable across empty and non-empty draws', and packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/functional/_collate.py documents empty batches as arising 'from any Poisson-style sampler'. fun.py:14-16 does call these 'stable, supported public API'. Reproduced with the repo venv: clipped_fun(f, clipping_norm=1.0, batch_argnums=0) and auto_clipped_fun(f, R=1.0, batch_argnums=0) both succeed on a (4,3) batch and both raise on a (0,3) batch. One correction to the finding: the exception I observed is RuntimeError('cannot reshape tensor of 0 elements into shape [0, -1] because the unspecified dimension size -1 can be any value and is ambiguous'), not the IndexError('select(): index 0 out of range ...') the finding quotes -- the message is torch-version and function-shape dependent (the audit ran torch 2.13.0, the tree ships 2.14.0). The substance (fail-closed with an error that names neither the empty batch nor the API) is unchanged. Severity held at low and not raised: it is fail-closed, has no privacy or numerical consequence, predates the #856 delta, and the headline clipped_grad/auto_clipped_grad surface that ordinary users reach does handle the case. It is an API-consistency / error-message gap, not a silent defect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user composing a custom pipeline directly on opaque.api.engine.clipping.fun.clipped_fun or auto_clipped_fun (documented as 'stable, supported public API') with a Poisson sampler plus empty_collate gets an abort on the first empty draw. Reproduced on the current tree with the repo venv (torch 2.14.0+cu130): both factories return correctly on a (4,3) batch and both raise RuntimeError('cannot reshape tensor of 0 elements into shape [0, -1] ...') from inside vmap on a (0,3) batch -- an error naming neither the empty batch nor the API. The exact exception type/message varies with the wrapped function and torch version. Fail-closed: no privacy or numerical consequence, only a mid-run abort and an inconsistency with clipped_grad, which short-circuits the same input.

verdicts.title: tree_leaves still returns [] for a ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree -- the same silent fail-open shape #869 hardened in global_norm, in the same module
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly, line numbers unchanged. packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:126-127 is 'flat, _ = _ot.tree_flatten(tree); return [x for x in flat if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)]'; :377-400 holds the InputTypeError guard covering ClippedPytree, NoisedPytree, SecondMomentClippingOutput, SecondMomentNoiseOutput; the module header at :16 still reads 'Only tensor leaves are considered for tree_leaves and global_norm'. Ran all four side by side on clipped({'g': tensor([3.,4.])}, max_norm=1.0): tree_leaves -> []; global_norm -> InputTypeError('ClippedPytree global norm is unsupported ... Use `.pytree` ...'); tree_flatten -> ([ClippedPytree(...)], PyTreeSpec(*)); tree_map(lambda t: t*2, .) -> ClippedPytree(pytree={'g': tensor([6., 8.])}, max_norm=2.0). The three-way disagreement is real. One nuance the finding does not state: tree_map 'works' only because ClippedPytree overloads arithmetic operators and the wrapper is passed to fn as a single opaque leaf -- it is not registered as an optree node -- so a tree_map with a tensor-method callable would fail too. Severity kept at low and deliberately not raised: the documented contract of tree_leaves is that non-tensor leaves are ignored, and a bare wrapper at the root is a non-tensor leaf, so this is a hardening/consistency gap against the direction #869 set rather than a violation of a stated guarantee. No privacy or numerical consequence -- only a monitoring or parameter-count figure that silently reads zero. Not duplicated by any open tracked issue (the global_norm fix #869 / OPQ-333 is closed, and neither the milestone nor the other-open-issues list mentions tree_leaves).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user inspecting DP gradients calls tree_leaves() on the ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree that clipped_grad or gaussian_noise returns -- e.g. sum(t.numel() for t in tree_leaves(grads)) -- and gets [] back, so the count silently reads 0 (or a max() over the leaves raises a bare 'max() arg is an empty sequence'), with nothing pointing at the wrapper. Reproduced on the current tree: tree_leaves(clipped({'g': tensor([3.,4.])}, max_norm=1.0)) -> [], while global_norm on the same value now raises InputTypeError naming .pytree. No privacy or numerical consequence; this is an API-consistency gap, since tree_leaves is documented to ignore non-tensor leaves and the wrapper is an unregistered opaque leaf.

verdicts.title: per_group's own documented example raises for any model with 11 or more layers because substring patterns collide by prefix
verdicts.reasoning: All three cited lines verified at their stated positions in packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py: the Examples block at :116 is '>>> per_group(params, **{f\'layers.{i}\': norms[i] for i in range(32)})'; matching at :142 is 'matches = [pat for pat in all_patterns if pat in display]' (plain substring, unanchored); the multi-match ConfigurationError is at :155-162. Reproduced with the repo venv: 12 synthetic params named model.layers.{i}.mlp.weight with patterns {f'layers.{i}': ...} for i in range(12) raise ConfigurationError("Parameter path ('model.layers.10.mlp.weight',) (display 'model.layers.10.mlp.weight') matched multiple patterns: ['layers.1', 'layers.10']. Each parameter must match exactly one pattern."); the identical call with 10 layers succeeds; the trailing-dot form {f'layers.{i}.': ...} on 12 layers succeeds, confirming the proposed fix. Looked for an escape hatch and found none: nothing anchors or longest-match-resolves the patterns, and there is no doctest collection (no --doctest-modules or doctest config anywhere in the root or package pyproject.toml), so CI never executes the example. The example as literally written is in fact worse than the finding says -- with range(32) it fails on a <32-layer model with the unused-patterns error at :168-175 and on a >=11-layer model with the multi-match error, so there is no model size for which it works. Two small corrections to the finding's framing: the module docstring at :55-59 does state that patterns are matched as substrings of the dotted display path (what it omits is that one pattern must not be a prefix of another), and the raised error does name both colliding patterns, which is a usable hint. Severity held at low: fail-closed, docs-only, no privacy or numerical consequence. Not covered by any open tracked issue.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user copies the per_group Examples line shipped at _per_group.py:116 -- per_group(params, **{f'layers.{i}': norms[i] for i in range(32)}) -- to assign per-layer clipping norms. Because patterns are matched as unanchored substrings of the dotted parameter path, 'layers.1' is a substring of 'model.layers.10...', so on any model with 11+ layers per_group raises ConfigurationError naming the collision ['layers.1', 'layers.10']; on a model with fewer than 32 layers it instead raises the unused-patterns error. Reproduced on the current tree with 12 synthetic layers (fails) and 10 (succeeds); the trailing-dot variant f'layers.{i}.' succeeds on 12. Fail-closed and docs-only: the error message does list the two colliding patterns, but the shipped example is unusable on every supported transformer family and no doctest run catches it (doctest collection is not enabled anywhere in the repo).
